title: An odd move: answer it or ignore it
outcomes: Sorts an odd move into one that attacks something and one that threatens nothing
Replies well when the odd move attacks a loose piece
Sees when an odd move is harmless and carries on with the opening habits

steps.text: **They left the book: three questions** gave you the questions with labels. Now there is no label, and the first job is a sorting job. Does the odd move attack something of yours, so that a piece is loose? Then answer it. Does it threaten nothing? Then your habits are free again. A quick test: *if I passed, what could they take?*

Not every odd move is a threat. An early queen move or an edge pawn can look alarming and threaten nothing at all. Treat 'harmless' as a claim to test, not a feeling. Pass in your head, then look at every capture and check the opponent would have: does any of them win material or give mate? If none does, the move is harmless. Even then, ask what the move gave up.

steps.title: Answer it or ignore it?
steps.prompt: Black's odd move attacks a loose piece in the first position. Predict whether the second odd move also needs an answer, then check.
When an opponent plays something you do not know, which do you do first: look for what it attacks, or look up what it is called? What would you change?
